2026-12-16.title: Wednesday of the Third Week of Advent
readings: Let the clouds rain down the Just One, and the earth bring forth a Saviour
Go and tell John what you have seen and heard
2026-12-16.verse: And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.”
theo: “Shower, O heavens, from above, and let the skies rain down righteousness; let the earth open, that salvation may spring up.” This verse became the famous Advent chant Rorate caeli. Heaven and earth cooperate: grace comes down, and the earth (the Virgin's womb) brings forth the Saviour. God says, “There is no other god besides me… Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth!”

From prison John sends disciples to ask Jesus: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?” Jesus does not answer with a title but with evidence: the blind see, the lame walk, the poor hear good news, Isaiah's signs fulfilled. “Blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.” Even the greatest prophet had to trust a Messiah different from what he expected.
outline: Ask: what do you do when Jesus doesn't act the way you expect?
Point 1 · Rain down the Just One

live: Tell Jesus honestly any doubt you carry, as John did.

2026-12-16.prayer: Rain down, O heavens, the Just One; let the earth bring forth a Saviour. Lord Jesus, when I doubt, show me your works, and keep me from taking offence at your ways. Amen.
altar: At Mass the heavens rain down the Righteous One. The earth, our bread and wine, opens to bring forth the Saviour.

family.explain: John asked: are you the one we are waiting for? Jesus said: look at what I do: the blind see, the sick are healed, the poor hear good news.

pm.open: Rain down, O heavens, the Righteous One. Lord Jesus, as we gather, open our eyes to the signs of your coming and make our lives signs of your love. Amen.
share: John asked: are you the one who is to come? (Luke 7:20). What questions or doubts do I bring to Jesus?
What signs of Christ's presence have I seen this year?
How can my life be a sign that the Messiah has come?
pm.resp: Rain down, O heavens, the Just One.
interc: For the Church, that her works of mercy may be signs of Christ's presence.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick and disabled.
For those who doubt, that they may see the signs of Christ.
For the poor, that they may hear good news.
For our group, that we may accept Jesus as he is.
pm.close: Lord God, you sent your Son to heal and to bring good news to the poor. Let the earth open and bring forth salvation, and make us signs of his coming. Amen.

illus: A Hindu villager in Odisha was asked why he trusted the Catholic sisters who ran the dispensary. He said: “I do not know their theology. But I have seen how they care for the lepers no one else will touch. That tells me who their God is.”

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah proclaims: I am the Lord, and there is no other. Shower, O heavens, from above, and let the skies rain down righteousness; let the earth open, that salvation may spring up (Isaiah 45:6, 8). The Church has sung this verse for centuries in Advent as the Rorate caeli: heaven drops down its dew, and the earth gives birth to the Saviour.
God says: turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear (Isaiah 45:22–23). The Saviour is for all nations.

In the Gospel John the Baptist, in prison, sends his disciples to ask Jesus: are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another? Even John had questions. Jesus answers: go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them. And blessed is anyone who takes no offence at me (Luke 7:20–23).
Jesus does not give John a theory; he points to signs. Isaiah had foretold them. Where the Messiah is, people are healed and the poor hear good news.

Today too, people ask the Church: are you the one? Is Christ real? The best answer is not argument, but signs: hospitals, schools, care for the poor, families transformed, sinners forgiven, lives given in love. Our deeds must show that the Messiah has come.

Blessed is anyone who takes no offence at me. Some were offended because Jesus was not the Messiah they expected. This Advent, let us accept Jesus as he is, not as we want him to be, and let our lives become signs that he has come. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus showed who He was by healing and helping people. We show we love Jesus by helping others too!
